title: Algebraic-closure coefficient change commutes with bounded-below direct image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use $E_Z=p_Z^*\underline E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Z}=p_Z^*\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ on $Z=X,Y$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], with the filtered-union condensed convention. For every bounded-below $C\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(E_X))$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], the canonical coefficient-change morphism
$$\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Y}\otimes^L_{E_Y}Rf_{*,E}C\longrightarrow Rf_{*,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}(\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes^L_{E_X}C)$$
is an isomorphism in the ordinary ambient module derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. The map is the adjoint of extension of the $E$-coefficient counit under the canonical pullback/tensor identification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. No constructibility or finite Tor amplitude is required.

proof.text: Choose a common scalar basis of the regular algebraic-closure coefficient module over E, using the finite-subextension-valued condensed convention. The derived scalar-basis theorem supplies central endomorphisms tau on every scheme, identifies each extension/restriction unit copower with an isomorphism on every unbounded derived input, and identifies the scalar actions before and after the actual derived pushforward. No direct-image continuity is assumed in this step.

Extract N with C in D^{ge N}. Apply bounded copower continuity for the qcqs morphism f to copies of C indexed by that same basis. Its result is precisely invertibility of Sigma.desc of Rf_* applied to the coprojections. This argument uses finite partial sums of one strictly bounded-below representative and qcqs filtered continuity; it imposes neither properness nor an upper bound on C.

Restriction of internal modules reflects isomorphisms by the forgetful module functor. Exactness and the natural homology comparison transfer this reflection to the derived restriction functor. The mate of the specified derivedPushHom is the inverse of derivedComapLowerStarIso, so it is invertible. The I-indexed copowers exist in both derived categories because a Grothendieck abelian module category has coproducts and its derived category inherits them. Apply the coefficient-push copower criterion to the two derived scalar adjunctions and the central basis endomorphisms. Their naturality and pushforward scalar compatibility verify the criterion's commuting-square hypothesis; the two unit copower maps are the isomorphisms of step 1 and the remaining copower comparison is invertible by step 2. Hence the actual derivedPushHom component at C is an isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 5.3(1) and 5.6; F5 reuses the proved scalar-basis and bounded-copower route already assembled for proper maps in Sheaf.UpstreamExtra.WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.ModuleObject.Colimit.Compatibility, observing that its only geometric input condensedSubfield_bounded_copower_comparison assumes qcqs, not properness.
